page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.metal-24xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized instance built on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The system features 96 dedicated physical ARM Neoverse-V2 cores operating at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 vCPU-to-physical-core ratio. The memory subsystem is populated with 192 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core, along with 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache.

Integrated directly into the host platform are 5,700 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a 40 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight the strength of its massive parallel hardware profile, with stress-ng multi-core performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and multi-threaded decompression all registering in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 481.5 GB/sec for uncached reads and 201.7 GB/sec for writes, complementing high-volume static web serving throughput of 103.56 GB/sec.

Single-threaded execution metrics, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core tests, rank within the middle 50 percent, reflecting standard ARMv9 clock speeds. The resource density provides solid cost efficiency for parallelized, non-hyperthreaded workloads where dedicated execution cores prevent resource contention. The 5,700 GB NVMe volume delivers the localized I/O performance demonstrated by top-tier results in Redis SET benchmarks (199.87 million operations per second) and PassMark database operations.

With its blend of high core count, high-bandwidth DDR5 memory, and large local NVMe storage, the c8gd.metal-24xl is well structured for large-scale software compilation, distributed caching layers, relational and NoSQL databases, continuous integration pipelines, and high-concurrency containerized workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.metal-24xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server featuring 96 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores at 2.8 GHz without hyperthreading. It provides 192 GB of DDR5 memory, offering 2.0 GB per core, and includes 5,700 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 40 Gbps network baseline. Synthetic and application benchmarks demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded processing, software compilation speeds, and database execution, including over 199 million Redis SET operations per second and 481.5 GB/sec uncached read memory bandwidth. While single-thread execution falls within typical mid-tier ranges, the dedicated bare-metal architecture removes hypervisor overhead and virtualization jitter. The platform delivers strong cost efficiency per physical core for parallel computing, distributed in-memory databases, large Clang compilation tasks, and high-throughput static web serving.
